question: A customer is angry because an item is faulty. What should you do first?
option_a: Walk away until they calm down
option_b: Listen calmly and let them explain
option_c: Tell them it is not your problem
option_d: Ask them to come back tomorrow
explanation: Listening first shows respect and helps you understand the problem before fixing it.

question: A customer asks for something you do not know. What is the best response?
option_a: Say you do not know and walk off
option_b: Say you will find out and then follow up
option_c: Tell them to ask someone else
explanation: Being honest and following through builds trust.

question: Which greeting is best when a customer walks in?
option_a: A friendly hello and an offer to help
explanation: A warm greeting makes customers feel welcome.

question: Two customers need help at the same time. What should you do?
option_d: Ask one to wait politely and tell them you will be right back
explanation: Acknowledge both so nobody feels ignored, then help in turn.

question: A customer thanks you for your help. What is the best reply?
option_a: Smile and say you are happy to help
option_c: Say it is your job and turn away
explanation: A friendly reply leaves a good last impression.

question: What is the best way to check that someone understood your instructions?
option_c: Ask them to repeat it in their own words
explanation: Asking people to explain it back shows whether the message was clear.

question: You are writing a short work email. Which opening is best?
option_c: All capital letters to show importance
option_d: A clear greeting and the reason for the email
explanation: A clear greeting and purpose helps the reader quickly.

question: A colleague is talking to you. What shows good listening?
explanation: Attention and small signals show you are listening.

question: You must explain a hard idea to a new person. What helps most?
option_c: Use plain words and an example
explanation: Plain words and examples make ideas easy to follow.

question: Someone disagrees with you at work. What is the best approach?
option_a: Stay calm and explain your view respectfully
option_b: Talk badly about them to others
explanation: Calm and respectful talk keeps the working relationship healthy.

question: Your team has a shared deadline and one person is behind. What is best?
option_c: Offer help or ask how the team can support them
explanation: Good teams support each other to meet shared goals.

question: Which shows good teamwork?
option_d: Doing only your own tasks and ignoring others
explanation: Sharing information helps the whole team.

question: Your team makes a mistake. What should you do?
option_b: Admit it and help fix it together
explanation: Owning a mistake together and fixing it keeps trust strong.

question: A teammate has a different idea from yours. What is best?
option_a: Listen and compare both ideas for the best result
explanation: Listening to different ideas often leads to better results.

question: The team succeeds. How should you respond?
option_a: Thank the team and share the credit
explanation: Sharing credit builds a positive team spirit.

question: You have three tasks due today. What should you do first?
option_b: List them and do the most urgent first
explanation: Listing and ranking tasks by urgency keeps work on track.

question: Your shift starts at 08:00. What is the best habit?
option_c: Arrive a little early to be ready
explanation: Arriving early gives you time to prepare.

question: A task is taking much longer than planned. What is best?
option_c: Tell your supervisor early and adjust the plan
explanation: Telling people early lets the plan be adjusted.

question: Which helps you avoid missing deadlines?
option_b: Working only at the last minute
option_d: Breaking big tasks into small steps with dates
explanation: Small steps with dates make big tasks manageable.

question: You keep getting distracted by your phone at work. What helps?
option_a: Leave it on the desk with sound on
option_d: Keep it in your pocket and check it on breaks
explanation: Limiting distractions helps you finish tasks faster.

question: A printer stops working. What is the best first step?
option_c: Check simple causes like power, paper and cables
option_d: Ask someone else to do it
explanation: Check the simple things first before trying bigger fixes.

question: You find the same problem keeps happening. What should you do?
option_a: Find the root cause and fix that
option_b: Fix it each time and move on
explanation: Fixing the root cause stops the problem returning.

question: You need to decide between two options. What helps most?
option_b: List the good and bad points of each
explanation: Comparing pros and cons gives a better decision.

question: You do not know how to solve a task. What is best?
option_d: Search for help or ask a knowledgeable person
explanation: Asking for help and researching are good problem solving habits.

question: A plan is not working. What should you do?
option_c: Review what is wrong and try a new approach
explanation: Reviewing and changing approach is part of solving problems.

question: A customer buys items costing R85 and pays with R100. How much change?
explanation: R100 minus R85 equals R15.

question: What should you do with a note that looks fake?
option_b: Follow your shop procedure and tell your supervisor
option_d: Hand it to the next customer
explanation: Follow procedure and report it so the business is protected.

question: Your till is short by R20 at the end of the day. What is best?
option_b: Report it honestly and check the records
explanation: Honest reporting and checking records is the right approach.

question: Why count change back to a customer?
option_b: To avoid mistakes and build trust
explanation: Counting back helps prevent errors and builds trust.

question: Where should large amounts of cash be kept during a shift?
option_c: In the till or safe as per procedure
explanation: Following procedure keeps cash safe.

question: Which key combination copies selected text on Windows?
explanation: Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.

question: What does saving a file do?
option_c: Stores your work so you can open it later
explanation: Saving keeps your work on the device.

question: What is an email attachment?
option_c: A file sent with the email message
explanation: An attachment is a file that travels with the email.

question: You cannot find a file you saved. What is best?
option_a: Use the search box in File Explorer
explanation: The search box can find files by name.

question: What is a web browser?
option_c: A program for visiting websites such as Chrome or Edge
explanation: Browsers open websites.

question: What does the formula =SUM(A1:A5) do?
option_c: Adds the numbers in cells A1 to A5
explanation: SUM adds the numbers in the range.

question: In a spreadsheet, what is a cell?
option_a: A single box where a row and column meet
explanation: A cell is one box in the grid.

question: Which symbol starts a formula in Excel?
explanation: Every formula begins with the equals sign.

question: How can you quickly find the highest number in a list?
explanation: MAX returns the largest value in a range.

question: Why use a header row in a table?
option_a: To label what each column contains
explanation: Headers make tables easy to understand.

question: Which password is the strongest?
option_b: A long mix of letters, numbers and symbols that is not a word
explanation: Long, mixed and unique passwords are hardest to guess.

question: You get a message saying you won a prize and must send your bank PIN. What do you do?
option_d: Ignore it and report it as a scam
explanation: Real companies never ask for your PIN. It is a scam.

question: What does two step verification do?
option_c: Asks for a second proof such as a code when you log in
explanation: It adds a second layer of protection to your account.

question: Is it safe to use the same password on every account?
option_b: Yes, if it has your name
option_d: No, if one site is hacked all your accounts are at risk
explanation: Reusing passwords lets criminals access many accounts.

question: A link in an email looks strange. What should you do?
option_d: Do not click and check with the sender another way
explanation: Suspicious links can steal your information.

question: A team member is struggling with a task. What would a good leader do?
option_b: Ask what is wrong and offer support or training
explanation: Good leaders support people so they can succeed.

question: How should a leader share tasks in a team?
option_a: Give all work to one person
option_b: Share work fairly based on skills and time
explanation: Fair sharing keeps the team motivated.

question: The team makes a mistake. What should a good leader do?
option_d: Take responsibility and lead the fix
explanation: Leaders take responsibility and guide the solution.

question: What is a good way to motivate your team?
explanation: Recognition builds motivation and trust.

question: Why should a leader follow the same rules as the team?
option_c: To set a good example for others
explanation: Leaders set the example for others.
